headings.title: Chapter administration, scheduling authority, and factors
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1) through (8), history note (L. 1971 H.B. 69 through A.L. 2020 H.B. 1896), and case annotations (State v. Winters, 1975; State v. Thompson, 1982). Assigns chapter administration to DHSS, permits adding substances after public notice and hearing, and lists eight mandatory factors to consider. Independent review revised title to cover DHSS chapter administration in addition to scheduling authority and the eight factors.

headings.title: Findings and rules controlling substances with abuse potential
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Directs DHSS to make findings on subsection 1 factors and issue a controlling rule if it finds a potential for abuse.

headings.title: Exclusion of precursors to immediate precursors
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Provides that precursors of a designated controlled immediate precursor are not subject to control solely for that reason.

headings.title: Mirroring federal scheduling, emergency rules, and objections
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4, history note, and State v. Thompson (1982) delegation annotation. Directs DHSS to mirror federal designation, rescheduling, or deletion via 30-day emergency rules under section 536.025 unless DHSS objects (staying control pending hearing and final published decision), and permits emergency rules to remain in effect until the end of the next regular legislative session notwithstanding section 536.025(7).

headings.title: Exclusion of lawful over-the-counter nonnarcotic substances
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and notes. Requires DHSS to exclude any nonnarcotic substance lawfully sold over the counter without prescription under the federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act and Missouri law.

headings.title: Controlled substance list filed with secretary of state
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and notes. Requires DHSS to prepare a list of all controlled substances and file a copy with the secretary of state.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 195.015:48808 (6 subsections including subdivisions (1)–(8) of subsection 1), history note (L. 1971 H.B. 69 through A.L. 2020 H.B. 1896), and case annotations (State v. Winters, 1975; State v. Thompson, 1982), and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked 536.025 emergency-rule mirroring/objection/stay procedures in (4) and federal OTC nonnarcotic exclusion in (5). Revised subsection 1 title to "Chapter administration, scheduling authority, and factors" to capture chapter administration; retained subsections 2–6.

headings.title: Criteria for placing substances in Schedule I
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1) and (2), history note (L. 1971 H.B. 69 through A.L. 2020 H.B. 1896), and State v. Burrow (1974) annotation. Sets the two findings required for DHSS to place a substance in Schedule I.

headings.title: Schedule I controlled substances
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 including subdivisions (1) through (9) and all listed opiates, opium derivatives, synthetic fentanyl-like opioids, hallucinogens (including marijuana/marihuana except industrial hemp, THC, and synthetic cannabinoids), depressants, stimulants, temporary federal emergency-scheduled substances (including fentanyl-related substances), and khat, plus State v. Burrow (1974) annotation. headings.title: Criteria for placing substances in Schedule II
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 including subdivisions (1) through (3) and notes. Sets the three findings required for DHSS to place a substance in Schedule II.

headings.title: Schedule II controlled substances
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 including subdivisions (1) through (7) and notes. Lists Schedule II vegetable-origin/synthetic substances (opium/opiates with exclusions, poppy straw, coca leaves with exclusions), opiates, stimulants, depressants, hallucinogens (nabilone and FDA-approved oral dronabinol solution), immediate precursors (phenylacetone, PCP precursors, ANPP), and alkyl nitrites.

headings.title: Criteria for placing substances in Schedule III
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 including subdivisions (1) through (3) and notes. Sets the three findings required for DHSS to place a substance in Schedule III.

headings.title: Schedule III controlled substances and rule exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 including subdivisions (1) through (8) and notes. Lists Schedule III stimulants, depressants (including FDA-approved GHB products and ketamine), nalorphine, limited-quantity narcotic preparations, buprenorphine, anabolic steroids (retaining archived source spelling 'metholone' in (6)(ddd) and cattle/nonhuman implant exclusions), synthetic dronabinol capsules, and DHSS rulemaking authority in subdivision (8) to except qualifying stimulant/depressant admixtures from sections 195.010 to 195.320.

headings.title: Criteria for placing substances in Schedule IV
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 including subdivisions (1) through (3) and notes. Sets the three findings required for DHSS to place a substance in Schedule IV.

headings.title: Schedule IV controlled substances and rule exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 including subdivisions (1) through (8) and notes. Lists Schedule IV limited-quantity narcotics (including tramadol), depressants, fenfluramine, lorcaserin, stimulants, butorphanol/eluxadoline/pentazocine, single-ingredient ephedrine, and DHSS admixture-exception rulemaking authority in subdivision (8); notes archived source cross-reference in (8) to 'any depressant substance listed in subdivision (1)' even though depressants appear in subdivision (2), retained without silent repair. headings.title: Criteria for placing substances in Schedule V
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 including subdivisions (1) through (3) and notes. Sets the three findings required for DHSS to place a substance in Schedule V.

headings.title: Schedule V controlled substances
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 10 including subdivisions (1) through (5) and notes. Lists Schedule V limited-quantity narcotic compounds, pyrovalerone, detectable pseudoephedrine/ephedrine compounds, specified depressants (retaining archived source '(25)' in (4)(a) for brivaracetam), and FDA-approved finished cannabis-derived cannabidiol products with no more than 0.1% residual THC.

headings.title: Nonprescription pharmacy sales of pseudoephedrine and ephedrine
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 11 including subdivisions (1) through (4) and notes. Governs nonprescription pharmacy dispensing, sale, or distribution of subsection 10(3) products: behind-the-counter sale by pharmacist or technician, minimum age 18, photo ID showing birth date, and direct delivery into purchaser custody.

headings.title: Electronic transaction logs for pharmacy sales
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 12 including subdivisions (1) through (4) and notes. Requires pharmacists, intern pharmacists, and registered pharmacy technicians to maintain an electronic transaction log containing purchaser details, amount, date/time, and dispenser name or initials.

headings.title: Pharmacy submission of pseudoephedrine and ephedrine sales data
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 13 and notes. Requires pharmacies to submit subsection 10(3) sales information according to DHSS transmission-method and frequency regulations.

headings.title: Prohibition on exceeding chapter quantity limits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 14 and notes. Prohibits dispensing, selling, purchasing, receiving, or acquiring quantities exceeding chapter 195 limits.

headings.title: Behind-the-counter placement of pseudoephedrine and ephedrine products
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 15 and notes. Separately requires all persons dispensing or offering pseudoephedrine and ephedrine products in a pharmacy to keep them exclusively behind a pharmacy counter inaccessible to the public.

headings.title: Section 579.060 penalties for subsections 11 to 15
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 16 and notes. Cross-references section 579.060 for penalties for knowing or reckless violations of subsections 11 to 15.

headings.title: Exemptions for liquid, gelcap, and prescription products
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 17 and notes. Exempts liquid and liquid-filled gel capsule preparations and prescription-only subsection 10(3) products from subsection 10(3) scheduling and subsections 11, 12, 14, and 15.

headings.title: Applications and rules exempting non-precursor drug products
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 18 and notes. Permits manufacturers or interested parties to apply to DHSS for regulatory exemption upon finding, based on law enforcement and evidentiary laboratory reports, that a product is not used to manufacture illicit controlled substances.

headings.title: Annual revision and republication of schedules
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 19 and notes. Requires DHSS to revise and republish the controlled substance schedules annually.

headings.title: Distributor security and storage rules for Schedule V under 10(3)
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 20 and notes. Directs DHSS rulemaking under chapter 536 for registered distributors' security and storage of subsection 10(3) Schedule V substances. Independent review revised title to scope rulemaking specifically to Schedule V substances described in subsection 10(3).

headings.title: Rebuttable presumption from required transaction logs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 21 and notes. Establishes a rebuttable presumption from logs maintained under sections 195.017 and 195.417 that the named person conducted the recorded transactions.

headings.title: Registration rules, fees, and section 536.024 compliance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, history note (RSMo 1939 § 9834 through A.L. 2014 S.B. 491), and effective-date note (Effective 1-01-17). Authorizes DHSS, after public notice and hearing under chapter 536, to promulgate registration and control rules and charge reasonable fees, subject to section 536.024.

headings.title: Registration requirement and three-year term limit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Prohibits manufacturing, producing, distributing, dispensing, prescribing, or wholesaling controlled substances without DHSS registration, and caps registration terms at three years.

headings.title: Scope of registrant authority and research activities
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Authorizes DHSS registrants to possess, manufacture, distribute, dispense, or conduct research with controlled substances to the extent of their registration and in conformity with chapters 195 and 579.

headings.title: Exemptions from registration and lawful possession
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 including subdivisions (1) through (3) and notes. Exempts listed agents/employees (excluding physicians, dentists, optometrists, podiatrists, and veterinarians), carriers/warehousemen, and ultimate users or lawful Schedule V/practitioner-order possessors from registration.

headings.title: Regulatory waivers of registration requirements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and notes. Permits DHSS by regulation to waive registration for certain manufacturers, distributors, or dispensers when consistent with public health and safety.

headings.title: Separate registration for each principal location
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and notes. Requires a separate registration at each principal place of business or professional practice where controlled substances are manufactured, distributed, or dispensed.

headings.title: Inspection of registrant and applicant establishments
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and notes. Authorizes DHSS to inspect establishments of registrants or applicants in accordance with chapter 195.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 195.030:10023 (7 subsections including subdivisions (1)–(3) of subsection 4), history note (RSMo 1939 § 9834 through A.L. 2014 S.B. 491), and effective-date note (Effective 1-01-17), and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked section 536.024 rulemaking requirement, three-year term cap, registration exemptions and practitioner carve-out in (4)(1), and regulatory waiver/inspection authority. Retained all 7 drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Applicant character and facility proof under 195.030
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1) and (2), history note (RSMo 1939 § 9835 through A.L. 2014 S.B. 491), and effective-date note (Effective 1-01-17). Conditions section 195.030 registration on proof of good moral character (or managing officers' character) and adequate land, buildings, and paraphernalia.

headings.title: Criminal conviction and substance-abuse registration bars
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Bars registration for controlled-substance misdemeanor adjudications/pleas within two years, felony adjudications/pleas within seven years, or current abuse of controlled substances.

headings.title: Public-interest standard and evaluation factors
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 including subdivisions (1) through (7) and notes. Directs DHSS to register applicants unless inconsistent with the public interest, listing seven mandatory evaluation factors.

headings.title: Scope limit for Schedule I and II registrations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes. Clarifies that registration does not entitle manufacture or distribution of Schedule I or II substances beyond those specified in the registration.

headings.title: Practitioner dispensing and controlled-substance research registrations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and notes. Governs state-authorized practitioner registration for Schedules II–V dispensing or research, optional waiver of separate nonnarcotic research registration, and state Schedule I research upon furnishing evidence of federal registration.

headings.title: Manufacturer and distributor registration by federal compliance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and notes. Entitles manufacturers and distributors complying with federal registration provisions (excluding fees) to state registration under chapter 195. Independent review revised title to scope the federal-compliance entitlement specifically to manufacturers and distributors.

headings.title: Grounds for suspending or revoking registration
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 including subdivisions (1) through (5) and notes. Lists five grounds on which DHSS may suspend or revoke a controlled substance registration.

headings.title: Disciplinary sanctions, probation, and reapplication bars
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and notes. Details permissive DHSS disciplinary actions (warning, censure, targeted limits, five-year restrictions termed 'under probation', up to five-year suspension/revocation, denial) and one-to-five-year revocation reapplication bars tolled by stay orders.

headings.title: Sealing, perishable sales, and forfeiture of substances
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and notes. Permits DHSS to seal a suspended or revoked registrant's controlled substances pending appeal, allows court-ordered sales of perishables with court-deposited proceeds, and permits state forfeiture upon final revocation.

headings.title: Early termination of registration restrictions or limitations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 10 and notes. Permits DHSS upon review to terminate prior restrictions or limitations if the registrant maintained compliance with them and local, state, and federal laws.

headings.title: Notification to federal Drug Enforcement Administration
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 11 and notes. Requires prompt DHSS notification to the U.S. DEA (or successor agency) of all suspension/revocation orders and forfeitures.

headings.title: Notice, administrative hearing procedures, and informal agreements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 12 and notes. Covers opportunity for informal conference, written notice of proposed discipline, 30-day Administrative Hearing Commission hearing request (31-day default effective date), 60-day DHSS complaint filing, and informal letters of censure/warning or restriction agreements without formal notice or hearing.

headings.title: Immediate suspension for imminent public danger
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 13 and notes. Authorizes simultaneous immediate suspension with subsection 7 proceedings upon finding imminent danger to public health or safety, continuing until conclusion unless withdrawn, dissolved by court, or stayed by the Administrative Hearing Commission.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 195.040:10025 (13 subsections including subdivisions in subsections 1, 3, and 7), history note (RSMo 1939 § 9835 through A.L. 2014 S.B. 491), and effective-date note (Effective 1-01-17), and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked two-year misdemeanor/seven-year felony bars, seven public-interest factors, Schedules I–V research registration, AHC hearing timelines (30/31/60 days), informal agreements, and imminent-danger immediate suspension. Revised subsection 6 title to "Manufacturer and distributor registration by federal compliance" to reflect party scope; retained subsections 1–5 and 7–13.

headings.title: Permitted sales to industry, pharmacy, medical, and lab buyers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1) through (4), history note (RSMo 1939 § 9836 through A.L. 2014 S.B. 491), and effective-date note (Effective 1-01-17). Permits registered manufacturers and wholesalers to sell controlled substances to manufacturers, wholesalers, pharmacies, listed practitioners, hospitals (hospital use only), and laboratories (scientific/medical use only). Independent review revised title to include manufacturers and wholesalers listed in subdivision (1) alongside pharmacies, practitioners, hospitals, and labs.

headings.title: Permitted sales to government, ship, aircraft, and foreign buyers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 including subdivisions (1) through (3) and notes. Permits manufacturer or wholesaler sales to government employees on federal exempt special orders, ship masters or aircraft officers without a regular physician on USPHS-approved orders, and foreign-country buyers complying with federal law. Independent review revised title to include aircraft alongside ships.

headings.title: Schedule I and II written orders and retention
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Requires duplicate signed official written orders for Schedules I and II, two-year preservation accessible to chapters 195 and 579 enforcement officers, and deems compliance with federal order-form laws compliant.

headings.title: Lawful possession in regular course of duty
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes. Declares possession or control of controlled substances obtained under this section lawful when in the regular course of business, occupation, profession, employment, or duty.

headings.title: Use limits for hospital, lab, state, and ship or aircraft staff
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and notes. Restricts in-state administration, dispensing, or use by hospital/laboratory heads, state/political-subdivision employees, and ship/aircraft officers to employment/official duty and scientific or medicinal purposes under chapters 195 and 579. Independent review revised title to reflect coverage of state/political-subdivision employees (not federal employees) and aircraft as well as ship officers.

headings.title: Registrant federal and state recordkeeping and inventories
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and notes. Requires chapter 195 registrants to maintain drug records and inventories conforming to federal law and additional DHSS regulations.

headings.title: Manufacturer and wholesaler production and disposition records
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and notes. Requires manufacturers and wholesalers to keep records of all narcotic and controlled substances produced, prepared, received, and disposed of.

headings.title: Apothecary receipt and disposition records
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and notes. Requires apothecaries to keep records of all controlled substances received and disposed of under this section.

headings.title: Record forms prescribed by the department
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and notes. Directs DHSS to prescribe the form of required records.

headings.title: Prescription dispensing requirements, retention, and refill limits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (RSMo 1939 § 9837 through A.L. 2019 S.B. 514). Governs good-faith pharmacist dispensing on prescription (except subsection 4 and Schedule V regulations), signature/electronic rules, patient/animal/prescriber details, filling endorsement, two-year pharmacy file retention, and six-month/refill limits across Schedules I–IV.

headings.title: Dispensing prescriptions from out-of-state practitioners
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 including subdivisions (1) and (2) and history note. Permits good-faith dispensing on out-of-state practitioner prescriptions complying with the other state's and federal laws, subject to section 195.080(4) quantity limits for Missouri patients.

headings.title: Sale of stock when pharmacy discontinues dealing
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Permits a discontinuing pharmacy's legal owner to sell controlled substance stock to a manufacturer, wholesaler, or pharmacist only on an official written order.

headings.title: Emergency oral prescriptions for Schedule II drugs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Permits good-faith pharmacist sale and dispensing of Schedule II drugs upon an authorized practitioner's oral prescription in DHSS-defined emergency situations.

headings.title: Mail and common-carrier limits for narcotics and hallucinogens
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Prohibits delivering narcotic or hallucinogenic drug prescriptions by mail or common carrier unless a bona fide physician-patient-pharmacist relationship exists.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 195.060:47912 (5 subsections including subdivisions (1)–(2) of subsection 2) and history note (RSMo 1939 § 9837 through A.L. 2019 S.B. 514), and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked Schedule V and subsection 4 exceptions, electronic prescription signature/retention rules, six-month/five-refill limits, out-of-state prescription 195.080(4) quantity limits, and bona fide relationship exception for mail/common-carrier delivery. Retained all 5 drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Prescriptive authority for physicians and listed practitioners
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (RSMo 1939 § 9838 through A.L. 2023 merged enactments). Authorizes physicians, podiatrists, dentists, certified optometrists (section 336.220), assistant physicians (section 334.037), and physician assistants (section 334.747), in good faith and professional practice only, to prescribe, administer, dispense, or cause statutorily authorized administration or dispensing.

headings.title: Advanced practice registered nurse prescriptive authority and limits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Governs certified APRNs (section 335.016, excluding CRNAs under 335.016(8); certificate under 335.019; collaborative practice under 334.104) prescribing Schedules III–V and restricted Schedule II (hydrocodone and hospice under 334.104), barring self/family prescribing and capping Schedule III narcotics and Schedule II hydrocodone at a 120-hour non-refillable supply.

headings.title: Veterinarian prescribing, dispensing, and supervised administration
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Authorizes veterinarians, in good faith and professional practice only and not for human use, to prescribe, administer, dispense, and supervise assistant or orderly administration.

headings.title: Prohibition on accepting unused substances and exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 including subdivisions (1) and (2) and history note. Bars practitioners from accepting unused controlled substances they did not originally dispense, except federally authorized delivery for patient administration (with recordkeeping and security) or section 195.265 disposal.

headings.title: Ban on personal-use prescribing or dispensing except emergencies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Prohibits individual practitioners from prescribing or dispensing controlled substances for personal use except in a medical emergency. Independent review revised title to cover dispensing as well as prescribing.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 195.070:54185 (5 subsections including subdivisions (1)–(2) of subsection 4) and history note (RSMo 1939 § 9838 through A.L. 2023 merged enactments), and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked practitioner cross-references (336.220, 334.037, 334.747, 335.016, 335.019, 334.104, 195.265), APRN CRNA exclusion and 120-hour supply cap, and unused-substance exceptions. Revised subsection 5 title to "Ban on personal-use prescribing or dispensing except emergencies" to include dispensing; retained subsections 1–4.

headings.title: Exemption for external-use preparations except coca leaves
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (RSMo 1939 § 9839 through A.L. 2019 S.B. 514). Exempts external-use-only liniments, ointments, and preparations preventing ready extraction from chapters 195 and 579, while explicitly retaining coverage for any preparations containing coca leaves.

headings.title: Initial acute-pain opioid supply limit and exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Caps non-veterinarian practitioners' initial acute-pain opioid prescriptions at a seven-day supply (subject to sections 334.037, 334.104, and 334.747), permits subsequent-consultation renewals, mandates patient quantity/risk consultation, allows documented medical-judgment exceptions, and exempts cancer, sickle cell, hospice/palliative care, licensed long-term care, and substance-abuse/opioid-dependence treatment.

headings.title: Pharmacist and pharmacy immunity under acute-pain opioid limits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Shields pharmacists and pharmacies from disciplinary, civil, or criminal liability for good-faith dispensing or refusing to dispense an otherwise valid prescription exceeding subsection 2 limits. Independent review revised title to include pharmacies as well as pharmacists.

headings.title: Schedule supply limits, physician increases, and exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 including subdivisions (1) and (2) and history note. Sets 30-day Schedule II and 90-day Schedules III–V limits, allows physician increases up to three months with documented medical reasons, and exempts out-of-state prescriptions dispensed to out-of-state patients and prescriptions dispensed directly to U.S. Armed Forces members serving abroad.

headings.title: Partial filling of Schedule II prescriptions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Permits partial filling of Schedule II prescriptions as defined by DHSS regulation.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 195.080:47913 (5 subsections including subdivisions (1)–(2) of subsection 4) and history note (RSMo 1939 § 9839 through A.L. 2019 S.B. 514), and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked coca-leaf carve-out in (1), non-veterinarian 7-day acute-pain opioid limit, consultation, documented medical-judgment exception, and disease/care exemptions in (2), 30/90-day limits and physician 3-month increases in (4), and Schedule II partial fills in (5). Revised subsection 3 title to "Pharmacist and pharmacy immunity under acute-pain opioid limits" to include pharmacies; retained subsections 1–2 and 4–5.

headings.title: Federal identifying symbol on commercial containers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (RSMo 1939 § 9841 through A.L. 2023 merged enactments). Prohibits distributing controlled substances in commercial containers lacking a federal-law identifying symbol label.

headings.title: Manufacturer compliance with federal labeling and symbols
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Prohibits manufacturer distribution unless labeling complies with federal law and bears the subsection 1 identifying symbol.

headings.title: Criminal-transfer warning on Schedule II to IV labels
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Requires Schedule II, III, or IV labels dispensed to or for a patient to warn that transferring the drug to anyone else is a criminal offense.

headings.title: Manufacturer and wholesaler package labels and tampering ban
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Requires legible English vendor, quantity, kind, and form labels on manufacturer and wholesaler-prepared packages, and prohibits altering, defacing, or removing labels except by a pharmacist filling a prescription.

headings.title: Prescription container labels and anti-tampering prohibition
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Requires pharmacy/practitioner, patient (or animal owner and species), prescriber, and direction details on dispensed prescription container labels and bars altering, defacing, or removing them.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 195.100:54186 (5 subsections) and history note (RSMo 1939 § 9841 through A.L. 2023 merged enactments), and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked federal container/manufacturer symbol rules, Schedule II–IV transfer warning, pharmacist exception to package-label tampering in (4), and prescription container labeling in (5). Retained all 5 drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Forfeiture, destruction, and records of substances and paraphernalia
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1) and (2), history note (RSMo 1939 § 9845 through A.L. 2014 S.B. 491, Effective 1-01-17), and case annotations. Governs forfeiture and disposal after a Criminal Rule 34 or appropriate hearing, court destruction orders with sworn returns, and DHSS receipt/disposal records open to federal and state narcotic enforcement officers.

headings.title: Proceeds forfeiture, close-proximity presumption, and 513.600–513.653 procedure
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 including subdivisions (1) through (3), history/effective-date notes, and constitutional/burden-of-proof case annotations (State ex rel. Covers forfeitable exchange proceeds and facilitating moneys with an innocent-owner exception, the rebuttable presumption for close-proximity currency, and procedure under sections 513.600 to 513.653.

headings.title: Application of section 195.140 to children's property
